claims.text: Replacing EAM reference potentials with a DNN interatomic potential trained on extensive ab initio configurations will better represent the configurations of multicomponent high-entropy-alloy liquids and high-temperature disordered solids.
The DNN reference will improve reference–target phase-space overlap during thermodynamic integration.
The proposed method applies to multicomponent metallic HEAs in both liquid and solid states near and slightly above their melting points.
The DNN should be trained on a wide range of ab initio configurations from HEA liquid and high-temperature solid phases.
The method is applicable over approximately 0.6–1.0 Tm and at temperatures above 3000 K for refractory systems.
The applicable compositional regime includes equiatomic or near-equiatomic mixtures of five or more elements.
A DNN can flexibly map the underlying ab initio energy landscape.
The DNN will accurately capture short-range order and the full spectrum of configurations in high-temperature HEA liquids and disordered solids.
EAM potentials contain restrictive assumptions that prevent adequate representation of the relevant configurations.
Avoiding EAM restrictions will better align the free-energy landscapes of the reference and ab initio target systems.
Better free-energy-landscape alignment will improve phase-space overlap during thermodynamic integration.
The DNN reference will reduce the thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
The path-mismatch error may be about an order of magnitude lower than with TOR-TILD EAM references.
The resulting free-energy errors will be much smaller relative to direct ab initio calculations.
TOR-TILD EAM reference potentials constitute the conventional baseline for HEA thermodynamic integration near melting.
The approach will work best when a sufficiently large and representative ab initio training set covers the diverse liquid configurations.
Inadequately sampled training configurations or extremely complex chemistry may limit DNN performance.
The exact improvement will depend on training-set quality, representativeness, and the alloy system.
Failure to obtain at least a twofold path-mismatch improvement or to reach approximately 5 meV/atom agreement with the ab initio benchmark would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial-state field limits the target to temperatures near and slightly above Tm, whereas the conditions field extends applicability down to 0.6 Tm, which is materially broader than the stated near-melting regime.
